raw_case_text:
A 25 years old female from Afghanistan presented to the medical out patient department of Combined Military Hospital Quetta with complaints of cough for 2 years, and hemoptysis and left hypochondrium pain for the last six months. There was history of occasional fever but no weight loss. Her weight was 48 Kg. Breath sounds were diminished over right mid zone. She had received various medications including anti-tuberculous treatment in Afghanistan. Posteroanterior and right lateral chest x-rays (Fig 1) revealed a large dense round well demarcated opacity involving the mid zone of the right lung field posteriorly. Ultrasonography revealed large simple cysts in the right lung (Fig 2) and the spleen (Fig 3). Both cysts showed the classic double wall sign. The liver and the rest of the abdomen were free of cysts. Hemoglobin, total leukocyte count and differentials were normal. A large unilocular hydatid cyst was removed form the right lung through a posterolateral thoracotomy. Oral albendazole 400 mg b.i.d. was given for 5 days preoperatively and 4 weeks postoperatively. The splenic cyst (Fig 4) was removed six weeks later, preserving the spleen. The patient's immediate recovery was remarkable and her symptoms were relieved completely.
A 32 years male from Afghanistan presented to the surgical out patient department of Combined Military Hospital Quetta with complaint of upper abdominal discomfort and postprandial vomiting of 3 months duration. He complained of dark coloration of the urine and yellowness of the sclera for the last one month. The frequency of vomiting had increased over the last 2 weeks. He had lost approximately 5 Kg weight in the last one month and presently weighed 62 Kg. Physical examination revealed mild jaundice and an approximately 15 cm mass in the epigastrium. Barium meal was suggestive of a large radiolucent mass involving the head of the pancreas with enlargement of the duodenal curve and pressure effect resulting in partial duodenal obstruction (Fig 5). Ultrasound was suggestive of a large hydatid cyst, containing a few daughter cysts, involving the head of the pancreas. Hydatid serology was positive. Hemoglobin, total leukocyte count and differentials were normal. Liver function tests revealed serum bilirubin of 128 mg/dl, alkaline phosphatase 1248 u/l and ALT 38 u/l. At laparotomy there was a thin pericystic wall anteriorly and the cyst was removed relatively easily. No gross biliary leakage was seen. The region was drained and the abdomen closed. The patient made and uneventful recovery with complete amelioration symptoms, clearing of jaundice and normalization of the LFTs. The serum amylase remained normal and the drain was removed on the 5th postoperative day. The patient was given oral albendazole 400 mg b.i.d for 4 weeks as a prophylactic measure.

subjective.chief_complaint: Two patients from Afghanistan presented with cystic disease: Case 1, a 25-year-old female with a 2-year history of cough and 6 months of hemoptysis and left hypochondriac pain; and Case 2, a 32-year-old male with 3 months of upper abdominal discomfort and postprandial vomiting and 1 month of jaundice, dark urine, and 5-kg weight loss.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Case 1 experienced chronic cough for 2 years with occasional fever, followed by hemoptysis and left hypochondriac pain for 6 months despite prior empirical anti-tuberculous therapy in Afghanistan. Case 2 experienced upper abdominal discomfort and postprandial vomiting (worsening over 2 weeks) for 3 months, accompanied by dark urine, scleral icterus, and a 5-kg weight loss over the preceding month.
subjective.past_medical_history: Both patients were from Afghanistan; Case 1 had received prior anti-tuberculous therapy.
subjective.review_of_systems: Case 1: positive for cough, hemoptysis, left hypochondriac pain, and occasional fever; negative for weight loss. Case 2: positive for upper abdominal discomfort, postprandial vomiting, jaundice, dark urine, and 5-kg weight loss.

objective.physical_examination: Case 1 weighed 48 kg and had diminished breath sounds over the right mid-lung zone. Case 2 weighed 62 kg and had mild scleral icterus and a 15-cm palpable epigastric mass.
objective.routine_investigations: Case 1: Hemoglobin, total leukocyte count, and differential were normal; PA and right lateral chest X-rays showed a large dense well-demarcated posterior right mid-zone opacity; ultrasonography revealed large simple cysts with a classic double-wall sign in the right lung and spleen with a normal liver. Case 2: Hemoglobin, WBC, and differential were normal; LFTs showed serum bilirubin 128 mg/dL [umol/L], ALP 1,248 U/L, and ALT 38 U/L; hydatid serology was positive; barium meal showed a large radiolucent pancreatic head mass widening the duodenal sweep with partial duodenal obstruction; abdominal ultrasound showed a large pancreatic head hydatid cyst containing daughter cysts.
objective.advanced_workup: Case 1 underwent right posterolateral thoracotomy with excision of a large unilocular right pulmonary hydatid cyst, followed 6 weeks later by spleen-preserving excision of the splenic hydatid cyst. Case 2 underwent exploratory laparotomy with excision of the thin-walled pancreatic head hydatid cyst without biliary leakage.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnoses: Case 1 had synchronous primary right pulmonary and splenic hydatid cysts (confirmed by classic ultrasound double-wall sign and surgical excision), managed with right thoracotomy cystectomy, spleen-preserving splenocystectomy 6 weeks later, and oral albendazole 400 mg twice daily (5 days preoperatively and 4 weeks postoperatively). Case 2 had a primary pancreatic head hydatid cyst causing obstructive jaundice and partial duodenal obstruction (confirmed by positive hydatid serology, ultrasound daughter cysts, and laparotomy excision), managed with open cyst excision and 4 weeks of postoperative oral albendazole 400 mg twice daily, achieving complete resolution of jaundice and normal LFTs.
